_plugin_name: The plugin's name, as people see it and as its tools and skills are named: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Several plugins built from eunomai-business can live on one computer when their names differ, for example one for applications and one for web projects. Default eunomai-business. See docs/configuration.md
_plugin_description: What the plugin is for, in the plugin list. Optional
_comment: Copy to config.local.json (git-ignored), fill in, then run: python tools/build.py. Nothing here is secret: every client is public. Reference: docs/configuration.md
_workspaces_root: Where each user's workspaces (local clones) go; empty for ~/<plugin_name>-workspaces, one folder per plugin. ~ is the user's profile folder; %VAR% works too. Avoid folders synced by OneDrive and anything under AppData (Claude Desktop may redirect it). See docs/configuration.md.
_diagnostics: true adds diagnostic tools, validation skills and a hook log. Keep false for users.
_support_email: Where users send what the connector cannot resolve on its own. Optional, but without it users get the report and no e-mail link.
_specialist: How the specialist works. Languages: documentation and specifications, and code (defaults to the documentation language); technical terms stay in English. Code is written where a project declares it (.eunomai/project.toml on its main branch), or anywhere when free_development is on (allowed_technologies limits it; empty means any). See docs/configuration.md
_app_preview: true lets people see the real application on their own computer, through the connector, where a project declares it. It runs code nobody has reviewed yet, with the person's rights, outside any sandbox: read the risk in docs/configuration.md before turning it on.
_app_tests: true lets the specialist run a project's tests on the person's computer, through the connector, where the project declares [tests]: code nobody has reviewed yet, with the person's rights, for up to 20 minutes. Separate from app_preview. See docs/configuration.md
_message_style: Optional: the accent colour (#rrggbb) and the fonts of the page and e-mail of a request for a new project. Leave it empty for the neutral look. See docs/configuration.md
_deny: What the organization denies Claude, written like Claude Code's permission rules: Bash(<command>) anywhere (* for any text), Edit(<path relative to a workspace>) in workspaces. The reason is what Claude tells the user; the examples are checked by the build. Reference: docs/hooks.md

deny.reason: Node packages are not among the organization's technologies
dependencies go through uv and the project's lock file

_organization: What the specialist should know about the organization (what it does, systems that already exist), and which of its skills to use for what. These come before anything personal in a user's session. See docs/configuration.md
organization_context: Example Corp makes industrial equipment. Existing systems: an ERP for orders and stock, and an HR system for people and absences.

organization_skills.use_for: the look of web pages and applications

_platform: The git hosting: gitea. github and gitlab are refused by the build until the connector has their code (docs/configuration.md#the-git-hosting-platform)
